name: OWASP Juice Shop — Full Benchmark Suite
description: 20 challenges across 5 tiers: Recon, SQL Injection, XSS, Access Control, and Advanced. Requires Juice Shop running at http://localhost:3000 (docker run -d -p 3000:3000 bkimminich/juice-shop).

challenges.goal: Find the hidden Score Board page on OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000) that lists all challenges and their solve status. The page is hidden from the main navigation. Report what you find.
Find and read the Privacy Policy page on OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000). Report the key data protection commitments mentioned in the policy.

Inspect the client-side JavaScript source code of OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000) to find any hardcoded credentials, API keys, or sensitive configuration values that should not be exposed to the browser.

Enumerate the exposed /ftp directory on OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000/ftp) and find any confidential documents, acquisition files, or internal records that should not be publicly accessible.

Perform SQL Injection on the login form of OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000/#/login) to bypass authentication and log in as the Administrator user (admin@juice-sh.op). Report the authentication token or evidence of successful admin login.

Perform SQL Injection on the login form of OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000/#/login) to authenticate as the user Jim (jim@juice-sh.op). You may need a different payload than a standard admin bypass.

Perform SQL Injection on the login form of OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000/#/login) to authenticate as the user Bender (bender@juice-sh.op). Standard ' OR 1=1-- may not work; try alternative SQLi techniques.

Use SQL Injection against the OWASP Juice Shop API (http://localhost:3000) to extract the full list of user credentials including email addresses and password hashes from the database. Report all users found.
Use SQL Injection against the OWASP Juice Shop API (http://localhost:3000) to extract the database schema. List all table names and their column names to understand the database structure.

Perform a DOM-based XSS attack using the search functionality of OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000/#/search?q=). Craft a payload that executes JavaScript in the browser when the search query is processed. Report the payload and evidence of execution.

Find and exploit a reflected XSS vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000). Look for parameters that reflect user input without sanitization. Try different endpoints and parameters beyond the search page.

Find and exploit an API-only XSS vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000). The vulnerability is in an API endpoint that stores malicious content which is later rendered in the browser. Identify the endpoint, inject the payload, and trigger its execution.

Access the hidden Administration section of OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000/#/administration) without proper authorization. The page is restricted but the access control is broken. Report what administrative functions are available.

Exploit an IDOR vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000) to view another user's shopping basket. The API uses sequential basket IDs. Find and access a basket that does not belong to you. Report the contents.

Exploit a broken access control vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000) to submit feedback on behalf of another user. The feedback API does not properly validate the userId. Submit feedback impersonating a different user.

Exploit a broken access control vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000) to tamper with product data. Use the API to modify a product's description, price, or image path. The PUT endpoint does not require proper authorization.

Use SQL Injection against the OWASP Juice Shop product search API (http://localhost:3000) to find the hidden Christmas Special product that was removed from the regular product listing. Extract the product name and its description.

Exploit a Poison Null Byte vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000/ftp) to download a file that has a restricted extension. The /ftp directory has an allowlist of file extensions, but a null byte injection can bypass it. Retrieve the restricted file content.

Find and exploit a Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000). Look for endpoints that process user input through a template engine. Craft a payload that proves code execution (e.g., calculate 7*7 or read a file).

Find and exploit a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop (http://localhost:3000). Look for endpoints that fetch or preview URLs (e.g., /api/url-preview). Use SSRF to access an internal resource or cloud metadata endpoint.
